Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government data exchange systems. 25 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: ASYCUDA World digital customs management system launched January 2026 (UNDP/UNCTAD), replacing legacy 2007 system. Customs stations interconnected via secure intranet for data exchange. This represents a specific functional revenue/trade integration but is limited to customs and not a broad government data exchange platform.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Sole cited source (UNDP, Jan 2026) confirms ASYCUDA World customs system is now operational but explicitly describes it as a standalone intranet linking only customs stations, not a cross-government data exchange. World Bank GovTech Maturity Index confirms Eritrea has no government interoperability framework, service bus, or FMIS/TMIS data exchange with other systems. A separate tax administration modernisation (ErITAS/ESTAP, AfDB/IMF-funded) is still an internal-systems upgrade, not evidence of exchange integration. Downgraded from 2 (Planned) to 1 (Not integrated) because 'Planned' overstates progress toward exchange integration specifically, and no source indicates a plan to link tax/customs data into a broader exchange platform; flagged for human review given the fast-moving situation (customs system just launched Jan 2026) and absence of a fresher, dedicated data-exchange source.
